bib.title: Natural Language Processing with Python, Chapter 9: Building Feature-Based Grammars
bib.venue: O'Reilly Media (book chapter; year inferred from the O'Reilly NLTK book, not printed in the chapter text)

question: How can context-free grammars be extended with feature structures so that agreement, subcategorization and unbounded dependencies are controlled without multiplying atomic categories?
contributions: Replaces atomic grammar categories (S, NP, V) with attribute-value structures whose features can be shared across a production (agreement)
Defines feature structures, paths, re-entrancy, subsumption and unification, with NLTK's FeatStruct and load_parser for feature-based chart parsing
Applies the machinery to verb subcategorization, auxiliary inversion, slash-category treatment of unbounded dependencies and German case government

results.claim: Unification of two feature structures fails (returns None) when they share a path whose values are distinct atoms; unifying a structure with one it subsumes returns the more specific one.
results.setup: NLTK FeatStruct, fs0 = A='a' vs fs1 = A='b'
results.quote: Unification between FS0 and FS1 will fail if the two feature structures share a path

results.claim: Unification that specializes a path also specializes every path equivalent (re-entrant) to it, so shared values are updated at once.
The motivation for features is to avoid a massive multiplication of atomic categories: plural/singular and person distinctions are carried as feature values in one production.

limits: Purely a formal-linguistics tutorial: no parser is scored, no corpus is used and the grammars are toy-sized.
Nothing connects feature grammars to statistical or neural parsing; modern parsers learn agreement from treebanks and the chapter says nothing about that.
Code uses Python 2 and NLTK 2 APIs (print statement, nbest_parse).
Off-topic for a pillar built on trained pipelines; only the agreement-as-shared-feature idea touches existing notes.
practices: Use variables over feature values to make agreement between subject and verb a property of one production instead of many (9.1).
Put fixed feature values in the lexicon and require phrase-level values to unify with those of the children (9.4).
Treat unbounded dependencies with slash categories (gaps licensed by fillers) rather than separate rules per construction (9.3).

terms.definition: a dictionary-like structure of attribute-value pairs, atomic or complex, used in place of an atomic category
two paths in a feature structure sharing one value, shown by numerical tags in an AVM
a partial order in which a more general feature structure subsumes a less general one
the operation that merges the information of two feature structures or fails
a category of the form A/B marking a gap of type B inside A, used for unbounded dependencies
